mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.25% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day window are not statistically lower than during the pre-trend period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a labor market strengthening that boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises by > 2% in a month while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative despite the labor indicators meeting the trigger criteria (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 1% for two consecutive months indicates accelerating demand, which elevates expected future corporate profits and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the identified demand expansion period.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a sharp drop in consumer confidence proxy (not available in evidence - so omit) would not be valid; instead, a sustained rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 100.0 for three months suggests supply chain expansion that precedes S&P 500 gains over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative during the identified expansion window (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 273.0, it indicates accelerating inflation that the Fed is likely to counter with rate hikes, which depresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than during previous inflation periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a low unemployment environment where monthly pay growth (PAYEMS) exceeds 150,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) remains below 3.5% for 60 days creates expectations of wage growth that lift equity valuations and drive positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% AND PAYEMS > 150,000 for 60 consecutive days
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the low-unemployment regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-time spike in retail sales (not available) - instead, a rapid increase in housing starts (not in evidence) - so use GDPC1 again but different trigger: A 2-month consecutive rise in GDPC1 of more than 3% signals a demand surge that supports S&P 500 gains over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by > 3% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive (p > 0.05) despite the demand spike.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer confidence (not available) - alternative: When supply chain capacity utilization (not in evidence) - instead, a sustained decline in supply inflation pressure measured by a composite of GDPC1 growth and RSAFS (demand) crossing below 0.5 suggests softening demand pressures that allow equity valuations to recover, producing positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate - RSAFS < 0.5 for 20 consecutive days
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain flat or negative despite the supply-demand balance improving (p < 0.05).
